subject: Bugs to Nimble problem to define the model

messages.author: 937253792853878c
messages.subject: Bugs to Nimble problem to define the model
parts:
Dear Nimble users,


I am trying to fit a Compound Poisson-Gamma model for zero-inflated continuous data. I have a BUGS model script which works fine, but I wasn’t able to use it with Nimble. It might be a problem of indexing, but I am not sure. Here is the BUGS code:


model{
### Covariates
for (s in 1:n_obs){
lambda[s] <- exp(mu)*SV[s]
}

### Observation model
# Strictly positive Observation
for ( s in 1:n_pres){
ngis[s] ~ dpois(lambda[pres[s]])T(1,)
Y_a[s] <- rho_a * ngis[s]
Y[pres[s]] ~ dgamma(Y_a[s], rho_b)
}

# Zero Observation
for ( s in 1:n_abs){
proba[s] <- 1 - exp(-lambda[abs[s]])
Y[abs[s]] ~ dbern(proba[s])
}

### Prior
rho_a ~ dgamma(0.01, 0.01)
rho_b ~ dgamma(0.01, 0.01)
mu ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
}

I have also attached an example with simulated data and a Jags inference. I would like to test the convergence times between Jags and Nimble.


I would be grateful for any advice to run this model with Nimble.


Many thanks,


Jean-Baptiste

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Bugs to Nimble problem to define the model
parts:
Thanks for this question.

The nimbleCode function isn’t designed to take text input.  The two options are to read a model from a file using readBUGSmodel or to use nimbleCode with the code itself (not in quotes).  For example
M1_CPG_nimbleCode <- nimbleCode({

### Covariates
                                for (s in 1:n_obs){
                                lambda[s] <- exp(mu)*SV[s]

} ## etc
)

Since you are using the T(1,) notation, you will have to read the model from a file.

Or, if you want to enter the model directly with nimbleCode, you will have to change that line to

ngis[s] ~ T(dpois(lambda[pres[s]]),1,)  

(see section 5.2.8 of the user manual).

I see some naming inconsistencies further down in your code, but it looks like you got stuck before then.

Give us another holler if you’re still stuck after getting the model code set up properly.

Perry

messages.subject: Re: Bugs to Nimble problem to define the model
parts:
The problem seems to be not in the actual building of the model but rather in the model-checking routine that by default is turned on. 

While we look into that, please try nimbleModel with check=FALSE.  I am able to build the model and run the MCMC that way.

I note that your line for running the MCMC uses the uncompiled version (but I realize you hit an error before that).  Be sure to use the compiled version.

Let us know how the performance compares with JAGS.  We recommend using effective sample size (effectiveSize function in coda package) divided by run time.

I note that you are using the “zero Poisson” trick, but with NIMBLE you can provide your own distribution if you’d like.

Also I note that this might be a model where some custom sampler choices could be useful.  Let us know if you want suggestions.

Send more questions.

Perry

messages.subject: Re: Bugs to Nimble problem to define the model
parts:
Regarding the error from NIMBLE’s model-checking step:

Daniel noticed that you provide initial values as a list of lists, in the style JAGS would use for multiple chains.  However NIMBLE wants inits to be only for one chain, so it wants simply a list of the initial values, not a list of lists.  

Specifically, in your code if you use init = inits_ll[[1]], then NIMBLE will use your initial values correctly, and that will allow the model-checking to be completed (i.e. with check=TRUE).

There is still an issue you have revealed for us to decide how to handle with model-checking in the case of truncation when initial values are not provided.  Thanks.

Perry

2015-10-22 16:25 GMT-07:00 Perry de Valpine <pdeva...@berkeley.edu>:
The problem seems to be not in the actual building of the model but rather in the model-checking routine that by default is turned on. 

While we look into that, please try nimbleModel with check=FALSE.  I am able to build the model and run the MCMC that way.

I note that your line for running the MCMC uses the uncompiled version (but I realize you hit an error before that).  Be sure to use the compiled version.

Let us know how the performance compares with JAGS.  We recommend using effective sample size (effectiveSize function in coda package) divided by run time.

I note that you are using the “zero Poisson” trick, but with NIMBLE you can provide your own distribution if you’d like.

Also I note that this might be a model where some custom sampler choices could be useful.  Let us know if you want suggestions.

Send more questions.

Perry

2015-10-22 12:30 GMT-07:00 Perry de Valpine <pdeva...@berkeley.edu>:
Thanks for this question.

The nimbleCode function isn’t designed to take text input.  The two options are to read a model from a file using readBUGSmodel or to use nimbleCode with the code itself (not in quotes).  For example
M1_CPG_nimbleCode <- nimbleCode({
                                ### Covariates
                                for (s in 1:n_obs){
                                lambda[s] <- exp(mu)*SV[s]
                                } ## etc
)

Since you are using the T(1,) notation, you will have to read the model from a file.

Or, if you want to enter the model directly with nimbleCode, you will have to change that line to

ngis[s] ~ T(dpois(lambda[pres[s]]),1,)  

(see section 5.2.8 of the user manual).

I see some naming inconsistencies further down in your code, but it looks like you got stuck before then.

Give us another holler if you’re still stuck after getting the model code set up properly.

Perry


On Oct 22, 2015, at 12:17 PM, Lecomte Jean-Baptiste <lecomte.je...@gmail.com> wrote:

Dear Nimble users,


I am trying to fit a Compound Poisson-Gamma model for zero-inflated continuous data. I have a BUGS model script which works fine, but I wasn’t able to use it with Nimble. It might be a problem of indexing, but I am not sure. Here is the BUGS code:



model{
### Covariates
for (s in 1:n_obs){
lambda[s] <- exp(mu)*SV[s]
}

### Observation model
# Strictly positive Observation
for ( s in 1:n_pres){
ngis[s] ~ dpois(lambda[pres[s]])T(1,)
Y_a[s] <- rho_a * ngis[s]
Y[pres[s]] ~ dgamma(Y_a[s], rho_b)
}

# Zero Observation
for ( s in 1:n_abs){
proba[s] <- 1 - exp(-lambda[abs[s]])
Y[abs[s]] ~ dbern(proba[s])
}

### Prior
rho_a ~ dgamma(0.01, 0.01)
rho_b ~ dgamma(0.01, 0.01)
mu ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
}

I have also attached an example with simulated data and a Jags inference. I would like to test the convergence times between Jags and Nimble.




I would be grateful for any advice to run this model with Nimble.


Many thanks,


Jean-Baptiste
